impact.affected_asset: Web Help Desk server process and its host operating-system execution context.

causal_trace.summary: An attacker supplies JSON to the AjaxProxy request path, including an escape-encoded spelling of the parameter key and a Java class-directed value.

The filtering logic parses JSON with Jackson and only recognizes a literal params key, whereas the subsequent custom JSONObject handling decodes \x escapes; thus the encoded key survives filtering and is later restored as params.

The surviving parameters are passed through AjaxProxy handling to materialize a supplied deserialization gadget; the writeup identifies a WrapperConnectionPoolDataSource/native readObject gadget. Independently, ZDI confirms that AjaxProxy deserialization of untrusted data is the mechanism for the related CVE-2025-26399.

The writeup characterizes the parser-differential bypass as RCE (CVE-2025-40553). ZDI independently establishes that the related unauthenticated AjaxProxy untrusted-deserialization issue, CVE-2025-26399, can execute arbitrary code as SYSTEM; it does not independently validate the newer chain's version scope or execution trace.

failure.operation: AjaxProxy processing of preserved attacker-controlled parameters into a native readObject deserialization gadget

primary_invariant.statement: AjaxProxy request filtering must evaluate parameter keys under the same escape-decoding semantics used by the downstream JSON parser, and must not permit attacker-controlled values to reach object deserialization.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The writeup shows Jackson checking only literal params while JSONObject later decodes \x escapes, allowing an encoded params key to bypass stripping and preserve a serialized object.

quality.review_notes: The primary writeup provides request and code excerpts but no standalone reproducer or captured execution result; its embedded demonstration is not treated as an observed run. ZDI independently corroborates only the related CVE-2025-26399 AjaxProxy deserialization issue and its SYSTEM impact. The supplied vendor artifact was not textually sufficient to verify an exact release or remediation semantics for CVE-2025-40553 or the authentication-bypass CVEs, so no fixed version is asserted for this record.

remediation.invariant_restored: All semantically equivalent spellings of protected request keys must be treated consistently before the request can reach object materialization/deserialization.
mitigation_classes: canonicalize and validate JSON keys using the downstream parser's decoding semantics before policy enforcement
prevent AjaxProxy parameters from reaching unsafe object deserialization
